page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance within the General Purpose family, utilizing a 1:2 ratio of vCPUs to memory. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, the configuration provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8).

The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, relying on remote network storage for persistent disk needs. Network integration includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel execution and memory throughput. Geekbench multi-core testing reached 16,160.0, placing it in the top 25 percent of evaluated systems, alongside strong results in image processing and Passmark physics simulations. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated high throughput, achieving 227.19 GB/sec read and 104.22 GB/sec write. Single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1,900.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,564.78, remain in the middle tier. Network web serving throughput achieved a high rate of 49.77 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 105.15 GB/sec.

Given the compute-heavy ratio and AMX support, the instance delivers solid compute density and throughput for CPU-bound tasks without the cost overhead of attached GPUs or excess RAM. It is suitable for batch processing, web serving fleets, image manipulation, software compilation, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-32 is a compute-oriented virtual server configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 16 physical Intel cores and 64.0 GB of memory. The instance features a 260 MB L3 cache and hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It includes zero local disk storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show upper-quartile performance in multi-core metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,160.0, static web serving throughput of 49.77 GB/sec, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 227.19 GB/sec. Single-threaded metrics and cache-bound operations register within the median tier. The instance is suited for compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks, including web serving, batch data transformation, and CPU-based matrix processing.
